newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen $1.50 higher, Brent five cents up.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen $1.50 higher, Brent five cents up.

text.p: IPE oil futures were called to open higher on Tuesday on stronger Brent values in Asia and a firmer U.S. crude overnight, traders said.
Front-month July gas oil futures were expected to start around $1.50 a tonne higher than its Monday settlement of $160.25.
August Brent crude futures were expected to open around five cents higher than its Monday settlement of $17.98 a barrel.
Brokers said London rallied at the close on Monday after NYMEX August crude broke above resistance at $19.04.

August Brent on SIMEX last traded at $18.06, eight cents higher than the London settlement as London's market-on-close buying spilled over into Asia. NYMEX crude on ACCESS last traded at $19.26 a barrel, 12 cents stronger than its close.
Brokers said Brent could test resistance at $18.15 if it was able to break out its recent $17.60/$18.02 trading range.
Gas oil is seen lamely tracking Brent ahead of the release of the API weekly U.S. stocks data.
Monday's firmer crude market tone drew support from a United Nations threat of more sanctions against Iraq.
Brokers said other factors could include U.S. market shifts in the run-up to the release of the API data, and possibly also comment by OPEC oil ministers meeting in Vienna.
Traders are expecting a rollover of the 25.033 million barrels per day (bpd) ceiling, a position endorsed by the dominant Saudi delegation.
The main focus of OPEC was likely to be how the group can rein in over production. Iranian oil minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh called for a stop to quota violations.
The latest Reuter survey of OPEC production, covering May, showed output at 26.95 million bpd, well above the ceiling.
